III. Probable Adverse Environmental Effects Which Cannot Be Avoided Should the Proposal Be Implemented
The principal impact on the immediate ecological system will be the loss of cover and food for the wild birds and other fauna which depend on the plants. The loss of these plants will likely also cause changes in the local insect population including any wild bees, and in soil microorganisms.
The chemical 2, 4D is only slightly toxic to people and animals, and in the recommended dosages not expected to cause any illness or injury.

The material lasts for 7- 126 days in the environment, as it is metabolized by soil organisms, with minimal damage to them, and usually disappears rapidly. No other adverse effects are anticipated.
IV. Alternatives to the Proposed Action
a. Burning of the Hemp. This is not a feasible alternative since the acreage involved is mostly muck land which would burn continuously and would lead to increased air pollution.
b. Mowing or Tillage of the Acreage. The area is inaccessible to road equipment.
c. Improved Law Enforcement Measures to Arrest Trespassers and Provide High Visibility Patrol of Property. The law enforcement personnel necessary to patrol 65 acres of land is presently unavailable. It is estimated that only 10 percent of the pickers can be stopped with existing force.
d. Legalization of Marijuana. This is not a viable alternative since removal of legal sanctions is not within the control of this agency. Even if legislation were to be enacted by the State of Indiana or the Federal Government, enactment would not be possible within the time frame necessary to keep this marijuana crop from being illegal.
